parts.name: body shell

physics.Basic_description: Red-painted metal shell forming the head and structural frame of the wrench, visible at the ends and around the grip.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the main structural integrity and houses the adjustment mechanism for the jaws.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by the head or the exposed metal sections near the handle ends for leverage.
physics.reason: Modeled as a shell enclosing the internal mechanism and grip, typical of cast or forged tool bodies which are not solid blocks throughout.

parts.description: Red-painted metal shell forming the head and structural frame of the wrench, visible at the ends and around the grip.
parts.function: Provides the main structural integrity and houses the adjustment mechanism for the jaws.

parts.name: wood grip

physics.Basic_description: Long, cylindrical red handle grip, appearing to be painted wood or a wood-composite material.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable and insulated surface for the user to hold and apply torque.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary grasp point for a robot gripper, offering a long cylindrical surface for stable holding.
physics.reason: Handle grips on tools are typically solid rods or dense cores to withstand torsional stress without collapsing.

parts.description: Long, cylindrical red handle grip, appearing to be painted wood or a wood-composite material.
parts.function: Provides a comfortable and insulated surface for the user to hold and apply torque.

parts.name: ferrule collar

physics.Basic_description: Small blue-colored metal ring or collar located where the handle meets the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Reinforces the connection between the handle and the head, preventing splitting or loosening.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to be a primary grasp point; usually avoided during manipulation.
physics.reason: Ferrules are typically solid or thick-walled rings designed for structural reinforcement.

parts.description: Small blue-colored metal ring or collar located where the handle meets the wrench head.

parts.name: butt cap

physics.Basic_description: Yellow-colored metal cap at the very end of the handle, opposite the jaws.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the end of the handle and may serve as a hanging point or striking surface.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping due to its small size and terminal position.
physics.reason: End caps are often thin stamped or cast shells fitted over the handle end.

parts.description: Yellow-colored metal cap at the very end of the handle, opposite the jaws.

parts.name: jaw shell

physics.Basic_description: Orange-colored metal jaw component that slides to adjust the wrench opening width.
physics.Functional_description: Moves linearly to clamp onto nuts or bolts of varying sizes.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to manually adjust the jaw width, though care must be taken not to pinch.
physics.reason: Jaws must be solid metal to withstand high compressive forces without deforming.

parts.description: Orange-colored metal jaw component that slides to adjust the wrench opening width.
parts.function: Moves linearly to clamp onto nuts or bolts of varying sizes.

parts.name: lever shell

physics.Basic_description: Purple-colored metal lever or worm gear housing used to adjust the movable jaw.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated by the thumb to drive the screw mechanism that moves the jaw.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasped with fingertips or a fine gripper to rotate and adjust the wrench size.
physics.reason: Adjustment mechanisms are typically solid or thick-cast to transmit torque effectively.

parts.description: Purple-colored metal lever or worm gear housing used to adjust the movable jaw.
parts.function: Rotated by the thumb to drive the screw mechanism that moves the jaw.

parts.name: grip ridge 0

physics.Basic_description: Cyan-colored textured ridges on the thumb lever, likely rubber or soft plastic for grip.
physics.Functional_description: Increases friction for the thumb to easily rotate the adjustment lever.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and textured for a standard gripper to target specifically; part of the lever assembly.
physics.reason: Grip textures are typically solid molded features or thin solid layers adhered to the surface.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
